doc.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Being named an NEA Jazz Master and closing
summary: He says he contested the title 'master' and prefers 'note worthy'; the interview ends.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: I’ll leave you with all of this stuff and you can bask in it. Before we wrap up, I would be remiss if I didn’t say that of course you’ve been designated an NEA Jazz Master in the last couple years.

I said I really don’t feel like I qualify as a jazz “master”. . . the Italian people refer to me as a jazz “maestro” and I like that better. It sounds more friendly and more meaningful. But I looked up the word “master” and I saw “eminent” as one expression and that sounded like a Rock n Roll guy. I didn’t like that one, “eminent.” Then I got “note worthy” and I accept that as instead of being a “master” I’m “note worthy”; worthy of the notes.
I don’t think we could have a better summation of this interview than that, do you Ken?
So why don’t we at this point bid the folks adieu.
Thank you very much folks and keep listening.
